# Cirth v0.8.1

Cirth v0.8.1 closes out four items from the M5/M6 upstream-issue audit:
zero-JS form validation feedback via `:user-invalid`/`:user-valid`, a
non-blocking "not ready yet" hint on submit buttons in invalid forms, a
switch-thumb color fix, and a fix for the group component hijacking
semantically-grouped elements. **The group fix is a breaking change** for
the default build.

## Breaking changes

- **The group component (`.group`) needs an explicit class in the default
  build.** `[role="group"]` alone used to be the trigger for the
  joined-controls layout, which meant any element grouped purely for
  accessibility reasons — most notably an explicit `<fieldset
  role="group">`, where the role is redundant since a fieldset's implicit
  role is already `group` — got hijacked into decorative styling it never
  asked for, making a semantic group and a decorative one visually
  indistinguishable (WCAG 3.2.4, Consistent Identification). Add
  `class="group"` alongside `role="group"` to keep the layout. The
  classless build has no class to require, so it keeps `[role="group"]`
  as its sole opt-in, but now excludes `fieldset` specifically.
  `[role="search"]` is unaffected.

## Added

- **`:user-invalid`/`:user-valid` support for form validation styling.**
  Text-like `input`/`select`/`textarea` pick up the same border color,
  icon, focus ring, and helper-text color as `[aria-invalid]` once a field
  has been interacted with and the browser has checked it against its
  native constraints — no JS setting the attribute. An explicit
  `aria-invalid` always wins. Degrades silently on browsers without
  support (Chrome/Edge < 119, Safari < 16.5).
- **Disabled-look for a submit button in an invalid form.** A
  submit-acting button inside a `form:invalid` drops to
  `--cirth-opacity-disabled`, but stays fully clickable and focusable — no
  `[disabled]`, no `pointer-events: none`, no ARIA state. A truly disabled
  button can never trigger the browser's own constraint-validation
  messages, since those only fire on a submit attempt; leaving it operable
  keeps that zero-JS feedback working.

## Changed

- **Switch thumb color now follows `--cirth-primary-inverse`** instead of
  a hardcoded white, matching the token buttons use for their own text. No
  visual change in the shipped theme (both resolve to white today,
  verified ≥ 3:1 against both switch tracks per WCAG 1.4.11); only matters
  if you customize `--cirth-primary-inverse`.

See the [Changelog](https://github.com/cirthcss/cirth/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#081---2026-08-10)
for the complete, itemized list.
